q: Which command copies only the contents of photos into backup: rsync -a photos backup/ or rsync -a photos/ backup/?
expl: The slash after the source means its contents. Without it, you get backup slash photos.

q: Before running rsync with --delete for the first time, what should you add?
expl: -n shows every deletion and changes nothing. Run for real only when the list looks right.

q: Type an `rsync` command that copies the contents of `photos` into `/tmp/q03/` in archive mode and prints one line for every file it transfers.
expl: `-a` is archive mode and `-i` itemizes the changes; the slash after `photos` copies its contents, not the folder.

q: `old.txt` was deleted from `photos`. Type the `rsync` command that only previews (changes nothing) what it would delete in `backup/` to match `photos/`, with one line per change.
expl: `-n` (`--dry-run`) only shows what would happen, so `old.txt` is still in the backup afterwards.

q: `backup` is an up-to-date copy of `photos`. Then `echo "Day 2: rain" >> photos/notes.txt`. What does this print?
expl: Only the changed file is sent: `f` for file, `s` for size, `t` for time. The pictures didn't change, so rsync skips them.

q: `copy2` was made with `rsync -a photos copy2/` (no slash). Now you run `rsync -a --delete photos/ copy2/` (with the slash). What happens?
expl: With the slash rsync syncs the contents, so `copy2/photos` doesn't exist in the source and `--delete` removes it. Dry-run first with `-n`.
opts: Nothing, the copy is already up to date
Only new files are copied, `copy2/photos` stays
`copy2/photos` is deleted and the files are copied straight into `copy2`

q: Does the slash after the destination matter: `rsync -a photos/ copy` vs `rsync -a photos/ copy/`?
expl: The destination is a folder either way. Only the source slash decides "the folder" vs "its contents".
opts: No, only the slash after the source changes the result
Yes, without it rsync creates a single file named `copy`

q: What does `rsync -a` keep that a plain `cp -r` doesn't?
expl: `-a` is archive mode: recursive, and it keeps times and permissions. That's why the next run can skip unchanged files.
opts: Nothing, it just compresses the files

q: Type an `rsync` command that copies the contents of `photos` into `/tmp/q09/` in archive mode, but skips every `*.tmp` file.
expl: `--exclude` takes a pattern; the quotes stop the shell from expanding the star before rsync sees it.

q: In the `-i` line `>f.st...... notes.txt`, what do `s` and `t` mean?
expl: rsync compares size and time to decide what to send; the letters show which of them changed.
opts: It was sent securely (s) over TCP (t)
Its size (s) and modification time (t) differ from the copy
It is small (s) and a text file (t)
